info.name: AM Platform
info.description:
Unified Postman collection for **am-platform** thin-layer services.

Import **this collection only**. Do not also import `AM-Identity.postman_collection.json` (that file is builder source and would duplicate Identity).

## Environments
| File | Use when |
|------|----------|
| `AM-Platform.local.postman_environment.json` | `npm run platform:dev` (localhost) |
| `AM-Platform.preprod.postman_environment.json` | Gateway at `am-dev.asrax.in` / `am.asrax.in` |
| `AM-Platform.prod.postman_environment.json` | Prod `https://am.asrax.in` |

## Identity login
Identity → **Auth** → **Login & Session** → **Login**: Web, Android, or iOS. Each sets `oauth_client_id`. Then **Refresh → Last login**.

Working OTP is Identity → **Auth → Web OTP**. `/auth/login/otp` is a 501 stub (**Auth → Deprecated**).

QR without a phone: Identity → **Flows → QR login (no phone)** (Start → Android login → Approve → Poll).

## Auto-capture (collection scripts)
**Pre-request:** fresh `idempotency_key` for meter/check POSTs; `X-Request-Id` header.

**Post-response:** saves `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `service_access_token`, `user_sub`, `subscription_id`, `plan_code`, `notification_id`, Google SSO vars, device-link and web OTP ids.

## Modules
| Folder | Service |
|--------|--------|
| Identity | am-identity |
| Subscription | am-subscription |
| Notification | am-notification |

request.description: Creates a user in Keycloak (admin API). Use a unique email per run.

item.name: Email verify and password
item.description: Mailbox verify and password reset. Codes/tokens come from email (or identity logs). Confirm endpoints expect exactly one of `token` or `code`.

request.description: Always 202. Sends branded verify-email if the user exists.
Set `verify_email_code` from email. Can use `token` instead of `code`.
Always 202. Sends reset email if the user exists.

Authenticated by current password, not Bearer.

item.name: Login & Session
item.description: Password login is platform-specific. Run one Login, then Refresh → Last login (uses `oauth_client_id` from the login you just ran).

item.name: Login
item.description: Web 7d TTL (`am-web-client`). Android/iOS 15d TTL.

request.description: Password grant as Web. Sets tokens plus `login_platform=web` and `oauth_client_id=am-web-client` (7d TTL).
Password grant as Android. Sets tokens plus `login_platform=android` and `oauth_client_id=am-android-client` (15d TTL).
Password grant as iOS. Sets tokens plus `login_platform=ios` and `oauth_client_id=am-ios-client` (15d TTL).

item.name: Refresh
item.description: Last login follows `oauth_client_id`. Platform folders pin the client.

request.description: Uses `oauth_client_id` set by the last platform Login.
Refresh using am-web-client. Run the matching Login first.
Refresh using am-android-client. Run the matching Login first.
Refresh using am-ios-client. Run the matching Login first.
Revokes the refresh session for the last login client. Expect 204.

item.name: Google SSO
item.description:
**Browser broker flow:**
1. **Get Google Auth URL** → open `auth_url` in browser
2. After redirect, copy `code` + `state` → **Google Callback**

**Flutter / mobile id_token flow:**
1. Obtain a Google `id_token` (see `automation/scripts/google-id-token.html`)
2. Set env `google_id_token`
3. Run **Google Token Login**

request.description: Returns Keycloak auth URL with `kc_idp_hint=google` and anti-replay `state`.
Exchange authorization code for AM tokens. `redirect_uri` must match the one used in step 1.
Same endpoint as Flutter GSI: exchange Google id_token for Keycloak/AM tokens. Requires `google_id_token` env var (1h TTL).

item.description: Collection Runner folders. Run top to bottom. QR TTL is ~120s; approve immediately after start.
